newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index falls, investors wary.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index falls, investors wary.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange share-index slipped 5.2 points on Monday and brokers said the market was likely to remain low with investors nervous about the economic and political situation.
The NSE 20-share index closed at 3420.02 with turnover slipping marginally to 27.1 million shillings traded on 541,759 shares from 27.8 million dealt on 672,750 on Friday.
"It is not affecting us," said a bourse official of violence on Kenya's Indian Ocean coast which has killed at least 33 people since last Wednesday.

But brokers said said the market was likely to remain low with investors watching political and economic factors closely since rallies in favour of political reforms began in May and the International Monetary Fund halted an aid package on July 31.
"Since May investors have woken up and no longer complacent about the investment decisions they're making," a broker said.
Athi River Mining (ARM) was the main feature of Monday, boosting volume by 120,000 shares as speculators flooded the market with shares on its second day of trading hoping to take a quick profit.
The share eased to close at 12.25 from 12.50, unchanged since its initial offer price in June.
Sisal stock Rea Vipingo was the only agricultural share traded on Monday, easing to 8.50 from 8.95.
Leading Supermarket chain Uchumi Supermarket was unchanged at 38.50 while national carrier Kenya Airways closed at 8 shillings.
Barclays Bank edged up by a shilling to close at 110 while Kenya Commercial Bank closed at 98 from 97.50. Standard Chartered Bank traded at 46.25.
Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 160 from 165 while Kenya National Mills gained a shilling to close at 40.
A total of 498.45 million of the fourth issue of Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded at 102.98 percent compared to 102.89 on Friday.
